items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: But we played the job for her.

ctx.x: After you studied, say a couple of years, when did you start playing any jobs with the real band, not necessarily professional, or that is to get paid for, but when did you join any small group or brass band? Can you remember what you'd say is your first job or your first orchestra?

Well, after I got the drum, as I told you, my uncle got the drum from a forum shop. I was going to Lansing. I had a fellow come to bring society notice to my house. His name was Lawrence Randall. He said, I told him I had a drum. He said, well, I got a trumpet. I'm learning how to play music. He said, I'm thinking about going to Old Man Chalini. And I told him it was a good idea to go over there. And so he said, of course, I've been getting a little lessons from my uncle, Joe Nicholas. I said, yeah? I said, yeah.…
I don't want to interrupt you, but I'll never think of it again. How was Faiso as a drummer?
